 Mexico coach in no doubt about Gimenez: “Much better!” 
 Go to the comments section Add to your bookmarks Share this article Mexico head coach Rafa Márquez left open the possibility of Santiago Gimenez starting against Jamaica in the first leg of the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-finals. At his pre-match press conference, he highlighted the striker’s improved spirits and reaffirmed his faith in him, stressing that the contribution he expects goes beyond goals.
 Mexico visit Jamaica at Kingston’s National Stadium in the early hours of Sunday, at 1am mainland Portugal time. With the tie set to be decided on Tuesday in Monterrey, a place in the competition’s final four and direct qualification for the 2027 Gold Cup are at stake. Against this backdrop, Rafa Márquez offered a more positive assessment of Gimenez’s current form, without guaranteeing him a place in the starting line-up.
 OneFootball Videos
 The striker’s mental progress was the first area singled out for praise. Márquez acknowledged his recent difficulties but highlighted a change in attitude, alongside the national team’s continued confidence in the player.
 “He hasn’t had the best of times, but today I see him as mentally stronger, with a different, much better attitude. These are phases players go through, but we have complete confidence in his work,” he said.
 The head coach framed the difficult spell as a passing phase rather than a reason to question the striker. His praise for Gimenez’s attitude suggests an opportunity could be coming, but does not confirm a starting place.
 As for what Gimenez could offer against Jamaica, the demands go beyond finishing. Márquez pointed to Club América’s Henry Martín as an example, explaining that he expects a broader contribution to the team’s play.
 “We hope that, if he gets the opportunity, he can contribute a lot, not just by scoring goals but by doing plenty of other things, like Henry [Martín, of Club América], who has scored a lot of goals, many of them penalties,” he explained. “But we believe Santi can give us much more. We hope he takes his opportunity,” he stressed.
 The message combines confidence with high expectations: Gimenez could get his chance, but he will also have to make the most of it through his work beyond scoring goals. With two objectives at stake in the tie, Márquez left his starting line-up undecided while making his expectations of the striker clear.
